B.court: Court of Appeal, Fifth District, California
B.holding_summary: In a fee dispute following litigation over a bed and breakfast in a single-family zone, the court held the neighborhood association was the prevailing party; the underlying ruling was that the voters' initiative rendered existing bed and breakfasts nonconforming uses that could not be resumed as of right.

quotes.text: Following the passage of Measure G, the operation of a bed and breakfast on the Kendall House property became a nonconforming use, such that [Real Parties] were not entitled to resume that use of the property as a matter of right, without regard to the rules governing nonconforming uses.
bed and breakfast facility operations -- a commercial use under the code -- are incompatible with residential uses

C.holding_summary: The court affirmed dismissal of neighbors' appeal for lack of standing, leaving intact the zoning board's decision that a homeowner's rental of rooms to college students fit the ordinance's 'family' definition rather than a prohibited boarding house.

quotes.text: Yoder rented rooms in her home to college students, but she discontinued the practice after the Township zoning administrator advised her that the use was considered a “boarding house” as defined in the Bethlehem Township Zoning Ordinance (Ordinance) and, thus, was not permitted in the LDR District.
The applicant maintains that the use is that of 4 unrelated persons living together and functioning as a common household in a single dwelling unit.
On February 25, 2009, by a vote of three to two, the ZHB issued a written opinion in Yoder’s favor.

D.holding_summary: Owner of row houses required by city housing code to obtain certificates of occupancy before renting suites stated a good taxpayer's cause of action challenging the commissioner's demand; demurrer should have been overruled.

quotes.text: requires “Certificates of Occupancy” for all multiple dwellings in the city as a condition precedent for offering any suites therein for rent
It is our determination that a cause of action is properly pleaded in plaintiff’s second amended petition
she was required to obtain Certificates of Occupancy for both of the aforementioned row houses before she could rent them

D.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
D.holding_summary: Whether apartments let for professional use retain residential character under the zoning resolution and are rent stabilized presents a question of fact precluding summary judgment; denial of the landlord's injunction is conditioned on tenants paying current rent and arrears.

quotes.text: use of these apartments for professional purposes is in violation of the certificate of occupancy and zoning resolution inasmuch as the building is zoned class A, residential apartments
There is a question of fact as to whether the professional use of these apartments is merely peripheral to a primary residential use
It is undisputed that each lease provides that occupancy is “for professional use only”

D.holding_summary: Conviction for permitting premises to be used by prostitutes was reversed because the jury was not charged that the State must prove defendant was owner, lessee or tenant of the house.

quotes.text: The appellant was prosecuted and convicted as being the owner, lessee or tenant of certain premises, situated in Dallas, which were knowingly permitted to be used as a place in which prostitutes resorted and resided for the purpose of plying their vocation.

before you can convict the defendant in this case, you must find from the evidence beyond a reasonable doubt that the defendant was either an owner of the house described in the indictment, or a lessee of said house, or a tenant of said house

D.court: District Court of Appeal of the State of California
D.holding_summary: A zoning ordinance validly barred an accountant's business from an R-4 'residential income' zone in which hotels, apartments, and rooming and boarding houses were permitted uses. The court treated letting of rooms as a residential income use identified with residential purposes, while affirming that such lodging businesses could lawfully be excluded from single-family districts.

quotes.text: The district is zoned for residential income uses and all of the businesses enumerated are identified with residential uses of the property.

It is therefore permissible to exclude from a residential income district businesses unidentified with residential uses, while permitting therein hotel, apartment house, rooming and boarding house businesses.
property may be improved and used for single-family dwellings, private garages, hotels, apartments, rooming and boarding houses

D.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
D.holding_summary: Campground leases limiting lots to a 'camp or summer cottage' unambiguously preclude year-round residency; the owner-association's lease restriction was enforced against lessees.

quotes.text: the lot of land hereby leased shall be used as a campsite for the erection and maintenance of a camp or summer cottage, and for no other use whatsoever
Supreme Court properly held that paragraph 7 of the lease as written precludes year-round residency in Ruback’s Grove.

D.holding_summary: In a use-tax dispute over motel reservation terminals, the court treated the furnishing of lodging by a hotel to transient guests as a taxable retail sale, but held the terminals used to make room reservations were excepted as property used directly in making retail sales.

quotes.text: “all transactions by which lodging by a hotel is or is to be furnished to transient guests” are sales
Since transient guests are the retail consumers of a hotel (motel), the retail sales of a hotel (motel) are within the definition of “sale” in Section 5739.01(B), supra.

D.holding_summary: In a suit for rents on a hotel/rooming house lease, the court held the lessee estopped to deny her landlords' title, but reversed for variance in the written lease and for excluding evidence of reasonable rental value during the hold-over period after an alleged substitution of tenants.

quotes.text: The property was used by the lessee as a hotel and rooming house.
the lessee was estopped to deny the title of her landlords ’named in the written lease under which she occupied the premises

then, in the absence of another contract fixing the amount of rents for the time Miss Lovelady occupied the premises after Mrs. Naylor vacated them, the measure of plaintiffs’ recovery for that period clearly would be the reasonable rental value of the property

D.court: Lancaster County Court of Common Pleas
D.holding_summary: Though a sublessee's goods on the demised garage premises were liable to distraint for rent, the landlord's personal judgment against the lessee was no lien on them and they could not be sold on that execution.

quotes.text: We agree with the contention that the property was liable for the rent due, and could have been levied on and sold under a landlord’s warrant. But the judgment was not a lien upon it.
it was provided' that it should not be sublet except by his written consent

E.holding_summary: Chancery held that a householder taking paying guests who contributed a proportionate share of living costs violated a private-dwelling restrictive covenant, though not technically a boarding house or inn.

quotes.text: Where the owner of a house permits persons to be guests therein, those guests paying proportionate share of the cost of their living, such use of the premises violates a covenant against any use of the premises except as a private dwelling-house.

I find that the defendants are not operating an inn or tavern, nor are they conducting a boarding-house, but I am convinced that the use of the premises as made by them is a violation of the restrictive covenants.

E.holding_summary: Chancery discharged contempt orders, holding that the injunction against operating a boarding house/hotel should have been stayed pending appeal because enforcing it would impair the subject-matter of the appeal.

quotes.text: the defendant should not be restrained from continuing to operate such boarding house or hotel pending the appeal,' because such .restraint will impair the subject-matter of the appeal
The right of the defendants to occupy and use their land and buildings for private dwelling purposes is not questioned

E.court: New Jersey Court of Errors and Appeals
E.holding_summary: Reversing a decree enjoining use of a covenanted private dwelling, the court held the decree did not conform to the finding that defendants were not keeping a boarding house. Incidentally keeping boarders in one's home is not a boarding-house business.

quotes.text: the test is whether the petitioners’ tenant occupied the house as a home for himself and his wife and children, and incidentally kept boarders also, or whether he occupied it as a place for carrying on the business of keeping boarders
The decree will, for this reason, be reversed.

E.holding_summary: Owner could not be cut off from sewer and water connections because she used her Sea Gate house as a boarding house; absent express restrictive covenants, boarding house use was not an offensive trade and could not be prohibited by the association.

quotes.text: a boarding house business could not be classed as an “offensive, noxious or dangerous trade or business,”
If it was intended to restrict the premises conveyed to strictly private residences or to prohibit the boarding house business, covenants to that effect should have been inserted in the deeds.

E.holding_summary: A lessee's taking in a lodger who paid a weekly price for a room, its furnishings and care did not violate the lease covenant against underletting or permitting others to occupy; the lodger was lawfully there in the tenant's right.

quotes.text: The plaintiff occupied a room in the premises leased to Mrs. St. Leger, under a contract with her to pay a certain price per week for the room and its furnishings and the care of it, which care was provided by Mrs. St. Leger.
It was decided in White v. Maynard, 111 Mass. 250, that such an arrangement with a lodger is not a leasing or underletting of the premises within the meaning of such a covenant.
We are of opinion that no breach of the covenant was shown, and that there is nothing in this part of the evidence to preclude the plaintiff from claiming in the right of the defendant's lessee.

E.holding_summary: A fire policy on a dwelling house was not avoided when the owner's tenant kept the house as a boarding house with a bar, because boarding houses were not among the enumerated hazardous trades. The court held the keeping of a boarding house was lawful and not a tavern, and the keeping of liquors for family use and sale to boarders was not 'storing.'

quotes.text: It is not a violation of a policy of insurance, that a house insured as a dwelling house was afterwards occupied as a boarding house, if boarding houses are not in the enumeration of prohibited occupations.
Aside from the unlawful business of selling liquor by small measure, it was no more than an ordinary boarding house, which she was clearly entitled to keep.
A tavern is a different house from a boarding house, or one where provisions are prepared and sold to boarders, or others calling in, for accommodation

E.holding_summary: A restrictive covenant against hotels and depreciating uses did not bar the club-house or the bathing use of the Robinson lot; the court treated operation of a boarding-house on a lot, and letting for pay, as not within the covenant's restriction.

quotes.text: There is nothing in this covenant that restrains business except of certain kinds. There is certainly nothing there which could bring any use within its terms simply because it was a use which could not be enjoyed unless it was paid for.
if the dwelling-house was occupied, as is one of the complainant’s, as a boardinghouse, it would be competent to erect on such lot, or on an adjoining one, bathing-houses

E.holding_summary: Mandamus denied to compel issuance of a hotel license for a former private residence; zoning barred rooming/boarding houses in the zone and the building code required fireproof construction for buildings converted to such uses.

quotes.text: Another ordinance prohibits the maintenance or operation of hotels, boarding houses, rooming houses or lodging houses without first securing a license.
Any increased occupancy of a frame building constitutes an additional hazard, as reflected by increased insurance rates.
Belators intend to offer sleeping and eating facilities to guests during the summer seasons, operating on both the American and European plans.

E.holding_summary: Conviction sustained for converting a building into additional living quarters in a zone restricted to a single detached house for one housekeeping unit; the ordinance's defective penalty clause was severable and did not invalidate the use restriction.

quotes.text: the premises here involved are located in an area designated as Zone A and restricted in use to “a single detached house used as a residence for one housekeeping unit.”

E.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
E.holding_summary: Condominium bylaws totally prohibiting leasing of units are enforceable and not an unreasonable restraint on alienation; owners who purchased gave up rights traditionally attending fee ownership.

quotes.text: The defendants in choosing to purchase the home willingly gave up certain rights and privileges which traditionally attend fee ownership of property
the prohibition on leasing is not an unreasonable restraint on the alienation of property

E.holding_summary: Certiorari dismissed; the District Court had jurisdiction to award the landlord possession against a holdover tenant, and OPA-compliance objections were not jurisdictional.

quotes.text: awarding to the landlord a judgment for possession of the leased premises against the prosecutrix
It is also urged that the written demand for possession did not comply with regulations of the Office of Price Administration.

E.holding_summary: An owner who rented rooms to lodgers and part of the house to a second family in a single-family zone was properly convicted; his claimed nonconforming use gave no protection because it had been begun surreptitiously and by fraudulent misrepresentation, and no occupancy permit could be obtained.

quotes.text: He acquires no advantage from the non-conforming use previously enjoyed where it appears, as here, that such use was surreptitiously and fraudulently effected.
he rented rooms to lodgers

E.holding_summary: The borough council's refusal of a variance permitting use of a large old dwelling as a rooming/boarding house in a neighborhood already dominated by such uses was arbitrary and capricious. The court set the refusal aside and ordered affirmative action by mandamus.

quotes.text: We fail to understand how a respectable occupancy that conforms to the prevailing use of structures in the neighborhood is contrary to the public interest; and we are convinced that unnecessary hardship would be entailed upon prosecutor were the resolution under review to prevail.

E.holding_summary: An agent having charge and control of a house who rents it knowing it will be kept as a disorderly house may be charged as owner and convicted of permitting a disorderly house.

quotes.text: he rented said house to one Minnie Clark, the mistress, of a bawdy-house, with full knowledge that it would be kept as a disorderly house and for the purposes of prostitution
In this case, appellant had charge and control of the house, and, for the purposes of this prosecution, he was the owner thereof.

E.holding_summary: A deed covenant limiting premises to 'dwelling-house purposes only' is violated by using part of the building as a meat and vegetable market, and will be enforced by injunction against a purchaser with notice without proof of substantial damage.

quotes.text: The above premises to be used for dwelling-house purposes only, with the necessary barn and outbuildings.
the use of any portion of the building for the purposes of the trade defendant carries on is á clear violation of the covenant

E.holding_summary: A conviction for maintaining a boarding and rooming house in violation of a zoning ordinance was properly reversed, both because the complaint rested on hearsay and because uncontradicted proof showed the same use predated the ordinance as a nonconforming use.

quotes.text: she also testified that the property is used now as it was before the passage of the ordinance. If that be so and her testimony seems uncontradicted then of course the ordinance was ineffective as to the respondent's use of the property.

E.holding_summary: Sewer rates chargeable per room to cottage owners, and per sleeping-room to hotels and boarding houses, were authorized by ordinance; the sewer attachment paper was only a year-to-year license, so rates could be raised.

quotes.text: For hotels or boarding-houses, seventy-five (75) cents per annum, for each sleeping-room, not exceeding thirty
I think the effect of that paper-writing and the conduct of the parties was to license the complainant to connect with the sewage system of the defendant at the prices therein mentioned.

E.holding_summary: The court dismissed the mother's partnership claim to two Cape May boarding-house properties, holding the daughter owned the realty and that the mother's occupancy rested on a lease at $3,000 a year while the boarding-house business was the mother's own. The owner's right to let the premises for rent and to retake possession on non-payment was treated as an ordinary incident of ownership.

quotes.text: the complainant agreed with the defendant Arabella Rogers to take a lease of the premises for the complainant’s exclusive use and benefit, at a rental of $3,000 a year
having failed to pay the third year’s rent, the defendant Arabella Rogers, in the spring of 1897, took possession and commenced business on her own account

E.court: New Jersey Court of Errors and Appeals
E.holding_summary: In a landlord's action for double the yearly value against a commercial tenant holding over after written demand, the court held yearly value is a jury question and that a tenant's bare assertion of belief in a right to hold over does not defeat the statutory penalty; judgment for the tenant reversed.

quotes.text: A tenant cannot relieve himself by the mere statement that he believed he had a right to hold the premises. He must furnish reasons sufficient to induce a jury or court hearing the case to believe he had a right to remain in possession.

This action was brought against á tenant to recover double the yearly value of the demised premises for a period during which, it is alleged, the tenant willfully held possession after the expiration of its term

E.holding_summary: An owner who knowingly lets a house to be used for prostitution cannot recover the rent; the lease is against public policy and void.

quotes.text: that the contract of lease was against public policy, and therefore void
it is the opinion of this court, that rent should not be recovered for a house knowingly let to a person who will use it, or who does use it, for the depraved and immoral purposes of prostitution

E.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
E.holding_summary: A zoning board rationally modified an owner-occupancy condition on a use variance so the dentist-owner could move away and rent out the second-floor residence; he need not re-establish the four-part hardship test.

quotes.text: Stewart, wishing to move to a larger home and rent the second-floor residence, applied to the Zoning Board for elimination and/or modification of the residency condition. Upon finding the existence of a “sufficient reason”, the Zoning Board granted his application.

E.holding_summary: Forfeiture of an inn and tavern license was set aside because the complaint failed to allege that the inn lacked ten spare rooms and beds, which would exempt it from the screen clause.

quotes.text: that court construes the statute as exempting hotels and “inns and taverns” which contain ten or more spare rooms from the operation of the “screen clause,” while subjecting to it the smaller ones containing less than ten rooms
The judgment of forfeiture will be set aside, with costs.

E.holding_summary: The zoning board's grant of a special permit for an owner-occupied supplemental apartment was upheld, including its reasonable interpretation of 'gross floor area' to exclude stairs and attic.

quotes.text: The board voted unanimously at that hearing to approve the special permit, upon the condition that the house be owner occupied.
The board’s interpretation here is, we think, entirely reasonable, especially given the relatively meager size of the maximum square footage.
Any one family dwelling in which a supplemental apartment is constructed shall not be used simultaneously as a Rooming House.

E.holding_summary: A variance permitting the owner to raze an old inn and build a motor inn in a single-residence district was annulled; the prior nonconforming inn use was irrelevant absent a bylaw provision, and neither the cost of complying with new lodging-house building laws nor the loss of a business sale was a substantial hardship.

quotes.text: A zoning variance granted with respect to an old wooden three-story structure used as an inn in a residential district in a town was in excess of the authority of the zoning board of appeals and must be annulled
the Legislature enacted new and extensive provisions relative to building laws applying to hotels, lodging houses, and the like

E.holding_summary: Where a lease restricted use to a dwelling and boarding and lodging-house and forbade subletting, a justice had no jurisdiction summarily to dispossess the tenant for breach of those conditions; the landlord must resort to ordinary process.

quotes.text: Where a lease provides that the leased premises shall be used only as a dwelling and boarding and lodging-house, and shall not be sublet, and also contains a provision that the lease shall be void if the tenant fails to perform on his part, a justice of the peace has no jurisdiction to remove the tenant by summary proceedings for an alleged breach of said conditions.

E.holding_summary: Taking of lodgers in a residence D district is a nonconforming, not a permitted, use; the summer hotel needed a special permit to alter, and the by-law aims to curtail and eliminate the taking of lodgers.

quotes.text: we think that the by-law as a whole discloses a pattern evincing a purpose on the part of the inhabitants to control, curtail and eliminate the taking of lodgers in some residential parts of the town
We hold that Harbor View’s use of its premises as a hotel, although lawful, is a nonconforming use.

E.court: New Jersey Superior Court, Law Division
E.holding_summary: An ordinance requiring a certificate of occupancy before selling or letting property was invalid as applied to a vacant, uninhabitable structure; conviction reversed and fine vacated.

quotes.text: the ordinance requiring an occupancy permit before an abandoned vacant structure may be sold does not bear a real and substantial relationship to a legitimate government purpose.
The right to possess property includes the right to dispose of it and the right of disposition is protected equally with that of ownership.
No owner or agent thereof shall hereafter sell, rent, lease or let to any person or persons, whether or not for a consideration, any dwelling, dwelling unit

E.holding_summary: Keeping an inn or tavern requires a license granted only upon a statutory application and freeholders' recommendation; the licensing body must determine the jurisdictional facts and hear objectors, and a license granted without such hearing is set aside.

quotes.text: When, application is made to Courts of Common Pleas for tavern license, under the Inns and Taverns act, jurisdiction to grant license in each case is acquired when the application is presented at the proper time and in the required form
If jurisdiction has been acquired, the power to license is discretionary and not reviewable.

E.court: New Jersey Superior Court, Law Division
E.holding_summary: A privately owned nursing home is authorized in a residence zone under ordinance provisions permitting boarding houses, hotels and eleemosynary institutions; the building inspector's denial was remanded for review under other regulations.

quotes.text: the purposes for establishing a nursing home are the same as the purposes for establishing a boarding house and hotel. They both provide lodging and meals for compensation.

It is my judgment that there could be no reasonable basis for allowing hotels and boarding houses and eleemosynary institutions and not allowing private nursing homes in a C residence zone of Belleville.

E.holding_summary: A boarding-house keeper who was wrongfully distrained upon by her landlord may recover double the value of the goods under the distress statute; damages for injury to her boarding-house business were struck from the verdict.

quotes.text: concludes with a claim of damages for disturbance of possession and hindrance in-carrying on her business of boarding-house keeper to the amount of $500
Judgment should be entered for double the amount found as the single value of the goods.

E.holding_summary: An owner's agent who knowingly rents a house for use as a brothel may be indicted as keeper of a disorderly house; letting with knowledge of unlawful use makes the lessor a principal in the nuisance.

quotes.text: The agent of the owner renting a house, knowingly, for the purpose of a brothel may be indicted as the keeper of such house.
The man who demises a house to be kept as a disorderly house, and which is kept with his knowledge, * * * may well be called the keeper of the house and be punished as such.

E.holding_summary: A boarding house keeper has no statutory lien under the Inn and Tavern act on the separate property of a married woman boarder whose husband expressly contracted and promised to pay her board. The keeper's acceptance of the husband's promise waived any lien.

quotes.text: A boarding liouse keeper lias not a lien, under section 68 of tbe act concerning inns and taverns, on the separate property of a married -woman boarding at the house
It extends the remedies theretofore had by innkeepers for the recovery of the- amount due to them for board by lodgers, by giving boarding house keepers like relief with them

E.holding_summary: Convictions for selling malt liquor without a city license were affirmed; the licensing scheme is valid, the burden of proving a license rests on the defendant, and an inn and tavern license granted to another does not shield an unlicensed saloon in the same building.

quotes.text: A license protects the inn keeper to whom it is given, but will not shield any other who may set up a beer saloon in a part of the licensed building.
to license, regulate or prohibit restaurants and beer saloons; to fix the sum to be paid for licenses

E.court: New Jersey Superior Court, Appellate Division
E.holding_summary: Conviction for zoning violation affirmed: the prior rooming house use had been abandoned after four years of closure and the present apartment use differed, so no nonconforming use protection survived.

quotes.text: In this case the use of the property as a rooming house was not actively maintained ; it did not continue after December, 1943, when Gaffney died.
He entertained roomers and paying guests; Mrs. Casper has three apartments there which she has ron ted out. Such a change or enlargement of the nse is fatal to its continuance.

E.court: New Jersey Superior Court, Law Division
E.holding_summary: A zoning ordinance limiting occupancy of accessory buildings to domestic employees of the owner or tenant of the main building was upheld, and owners were held in violation for leasing the garage apartment to others.

quotes.text: no accessory building over one story in height shall be used for residence purposes except by domestic employees of the tenant or of 1he owner of the premises.
Collins for leasing and permitting the accessory building to be occupied by a person or persons who were not domestic employees of the occupant of the main building

E.court: New York Supreme Court of Judicature
E.holding_summary: A tavern license is a personal trust that cannot be transferred with a lease of the house; the lessee selling liquor under another's license incurred the statutory penalty.

quotes.text: The defendant could not acquire any right to retail spirituous liquors under the license to Caswell. .This license is a personal trust

the commissioners of excise, in granting it, are not only to take into consideration the place where the tavern is to be kept, but more especially the character and ability of the person who is to keep it

E.holding_summary: A house of public resort where illegal practices are habitual is a public nuisance, and one who rents a building knowing it will be so kept is indictable as a principal; mere nonfeasance by the landlord, however, does not make him liable.

quotes.text: Any person who keeps, or causes to be kept for his own profit or amusement, or for any other cause, such a place of resort as I have described, or rents any building to any person knowing that the same will be so kept, is also guilty of an indictable misdemeanor.
Mere nonfeasance on the part of the landlord cannot involve him in the guilt of the tenant

E.holding_summary: A covenant in a lease not to let or underlet is not broken by an assignment of the whole term; restrictions on a tenant's power to part with the premises are construed strictly against forfeiture.

quotes.text: I think the covenant against an underletting was not broken by an assignment of the term
The courts have always held a strict hand over these conditions for defeating leases.

E.court: New Jersey Superior Court, Appellate Division
E.holding_summary: The owners' letting of rooms with shared kitchen and bath was found in fact to be a rental of a whole apartment, so the lower apartment rent ceiling applied and the statutory overcharge penalty was affirmed. Rooming-house registration could not be used to escape the apartment maximum rent.

quotes.text: separate sleeping rooms at the weekly rate of $10 each, with the privilege of jointly using the adjacent kitchen and bathroom, under a coexisting rooming house registration
Such a construction would make for an easy evasion of the remedial intention of the rent control laws, which are to be construed liberally in order to effect the purposes thereof.

E.holding_summary: A roomer-lessee of adjoining rooms in his landlord's home who accused the landlord's wife of theft in seeking indemnity made the statement on an occasion of privilege; judgment for the defendant affirmed.

quotes.text: the defendant, as a lessee of the plaintiff’s husband, was a tenant of several adjoining rooms in the home of the plaintiff and her husband
The defendant usually paid his rent on or about the first day of the month.

E.holding_summary: Keeper of a dining and rooming house convicted of keeping a house of ill fame; scienter not required because the statute is a police regulation for public morals.

quotes.text: The house, number 62 College Street, kept by the defendant, had been occupied by him under a lease from the owners for a period of some six years, and was kept and maintained by him as a dining and rooming house.

because this Act is a police regulation for the protection of the morals of the community, and it is reasonable to require that whoever in fact keeps a house which is a house of ill fame should take the risk of knowing the facts

E.holding_summary: A tenant's month-to-month arrangement permitting a third party to occupy part of the store premises for a monthly payment constituted a prohibited subletting, entitling the lessor to possession.

quotes.text: It was agreed. between the defendant and said Carroll that Carroll should pay the defendant at the rate of sixty ($60) dollars per month for such use and occupation, and that his occupation should be from month to month only.
This was a subletting within the prohibition of the terms of the lease.

E.holding_summary: A householder living in his two-family house with six or seven boarders got a permit to enlarge it for more boarders; the city's revocation 'in the interest of the public welfare' was set aside since the boarding-house purpose was disclosed and money had been spent in reliance.

quotes.text: which was used and is used by him as living quarters for himself and family, and. also as a rooming house, accommodating six or seven boarders.
The result is that the action of the board in revoking the permit is set aside, with costs.
his settled purpose was to occupy the house as altered as a dwelling and “boarding house.” If that be so, and we think it is, there was no fraud.

E.holding_summary: Conviction affirmed for maintaining a multi-family dwelling in a single-family zone; the nonconforming multi-family use had been abandoned by 27 years of single-family occupancy. Occasional boarders did not change the single-family character, since the ordinance allowed up to three boarders.

quotes.text: The fact that there were occasional boarders in the home during this 27-year period (who had their meals with the Reynolds family) did not change the character of the. use as a single-family residence, for under the Montclair ordinance up to three boarders are permitted at any one time in any residential zone without violation of the zoning ordinance.

There has been, instead, a change in the use of the property from a multi-family dwelling to a single-family residence and a constant, uninterrupted and active maintenance of the latter use for a period of 27 years. Such a change of use is fatal to its continuance.

E.court: New Jersey Superior Court, Appellate Division
E.holding_summary: Fire policy permitted five boarders/lodgers; the landlord's liability for a tenant's extra roomer turned on his knowledge and diligence under the 'no control' clause, and that issue should have gone to the jury. Judgment reversed and new trial ordered.

quotes.text: Boarders—Permission is hereby granted for five boarders, or lodgers, in the dwelling, or more than five boarders or lodgers, it being understood and agreed that in such case there is not more than a total of five bedrooms in the dwelling.

If, as the jury might properly have found from the testimony, the plaintiff had no knowledge and was not, by the exercise of ordinary care and diligence, chargeable with knowledge, then he would come within the protection of the clause.

E.court: New Jersey Superior Court, Appellate Division
E.holding_summary: The court upheld denial of a boarding house license for plaintiff's 28-room shore residence because the zoning ordinance restricted the district to single-family residential use. Scattered nonconforming boarding houses and a hotel nearby did not render enforcement arbitrary, and the prior rooming-house use had been abandoned.

quotes.text: On the ground that the use is prohibited by the zoning ordinance, plaintiff was refused a boarding house license for her 28-room, 13-bath residence at 936 Ocean Avenue.
commercial use of structures is prohibited and residences may be used “by not more than one family, for strictly residential purposes.”

E.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
E.holding_summary: Owners of a tenement house are personally liable for penalties under the Tenement House Law; the duty to obey department orders is nondelegable and cannot be shifted by lease to a tenant.

quotes.text: It is a duty which is personal to the owners, and cannot be delegated by them.
the defendants proved that they had leased the premises in question to one Kopel

E.holding_summary: Summer cottages built by lessees on landowner's leased land are an interest in real estate taxable to the record owner of the land.

quotes.text: The land on which each cottage stood was leased by the plaintiff to the owner of the building, by a written lease for a period of years. These leases all expressed that the land was to be used for summer cottages.
The language of the statute under consideration unmistakably indicates that it was intended to treat this kind of property as real estate, for the purposes of taxation.

E.holding_summary: Licensing authority has reasonable discretion to deny a license to keep a maternity hospital or lying-in place; mandamus denied.

quotes.text: no person shall keep a maternity hospital, or lying-in place, unless such person has previously obtained a license therefor
It must have been intended that the board should have some discretion in granting such license
